title: Managers Paid Above Team Average
description:
An `employees` table stores each person's manager via `manager_id`. Find managers whose **own salary is strictly greater than the average salary of the people who report directly to them**.

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| salary | INT |
| manager_id | INT |

Output columns: `manager_name`, `manager_salary`, `team_avg_salary` (rounded to nearest integer). Order by `manager_name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, salary INT, manager_id INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Ada', 200000, NULL), (2, 'Ben', 150000, 1), (3, 'Cara', 90000, 2), (4, 'Drew', 80000, 2), (5, 'Eve', 120000, 1), (6, 'Fay', 70000, 5);
solution_sql: WITH team AS (SELECT manager_id, AVG(salary) AS team_avg, COUNT(*) AS reports FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY manager_id) SELECT m.name AS manager_name, m.salary AS manager_salary, CAST(ROUND(t.team_avg) AS INTEGER) AS team_avg_salary FROM employees m JOIN team t ON m.id = t.manager_id WHERE m.salary > t.team_avg ORDER BY manager_name

test_cases.description: Managers whose salary beats the average of their direct reports

hints: First aggregate direct reports grouped by manager_id.
Join that aggregate back to employees to compare the manager's salary to the team average.
explanation: A CTE (or subquery) computes `AVG(salary)` per `manager_id`. Joining that back to `employees` on `id = manager_id` lets you compare a manager to their team. Ada's reports average 135000 (Ben, Eve); Ben's reports average 85000; Eve's only report is Fay at 70000. All three managers out-earn their teams.
